questions.stem: A supervisor assumes employees avoid responsibility and will work only under close control and threat of discipline. Which management assumption is being applied?
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Theory X assumes workers generally dislike work, avoid responsibility, and require direction or control.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Theory Y assumes people can be self-directed and accept responsibility under appropriate conditions.
Herzberg separates hygiene factors from motivating work content rather than assuming workers inherently avoid work.
Systems theory focuses on interactions among organizational components, not this view of worker motivation.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 21, McGregor Theory X and Theory Y, pp. 507-508

questions.stem: A company improves pay and working conditions, reducing complaints, but engagement remains low. Which additional action best reflects Herzberg motivators?
options: Increase meaningful responsibility, recognition, and opportunities for achievement
Replace recognition with stricter attendance monitoring
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Herzberg treats pay and conditions largely as hygiene factors; motivation is strengthened by achievement, recognition, responsibility, and growth.
incorrectOptionExplanations: More supervision does not address the motivating content of the work.
Disciplinary rules may affect compliance but do not create achievement or growth.
Attendance monitoring is a control mechanism rather than a source of intrinsic motivation.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 21, Herzberg motivational theory, pp. 508-509

questions.stem: In Maslow hierarchy, which need is addressed most directly by reliable guarding, stable employment practices, and freedom from workplace violence?
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Protection from physical harm and a stable, secure environment correspond to the safety and security level.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Physiological needs concern basic survival requirements such as food and rest, not primarily organizational protection.
Esteem concerns status, achievement, and respect rather than basic protection from harm.
Self-actualization concerns realizing potential after lower-level needs are substantially met.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 21, Maslow hierarchy of needs, pp. 505-507

questions.stem: Which practice best reflects management by objectives in a safety department?
options: Senior leaders issue broad slogans without measures
Supervisors evaluate employees only by hours spent in meetings
The safety manager makes all decisions without employee input
Managers and employees agree on measurable outcomes, responsibilities, and review dates
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Management by objectives aligns individual and organizational work through agreed, measurable objectives and periodic performance review.
incorrectOptionExplanations: A slogan lacks the specific, measurable outcomes needed for objective-based management.
Time spent is an activity measure and may not demonstrate accomplishment of agreed objectives.
Unilateral control conflicts with the participative goal-setting commonly associated with MBO.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 21, management by objectives, p. 510

questions.stem: A safety director uses a directive style during an emergency but a participative style when redesigning routine procedures. Which theory best explains the approach?
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Contingency theory holds that the most effective management approach depends on the situation, task, people, and environment.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Scientific management emphasizes task efficiency and standardization rather than adapting leadership to context.
Bureaucratic management emphasizes formal hierarchy and rules rather than situational flexibility.
Chaos theory addresses nonlinear and unpredictable systems, not simply choosing a style to fit conditions.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 21, contingency theory and management styles, pp. 510-513

questions.stem: Production incentives increase output but also increase bypassing of machine guards. Which response best reflects systems thinking?
options: Discipline only the last employee observed bypassing a guard
Examine how incentives, supervision, staffing, equipment, and feedback interact to create the behavior
Treat production and safety as unrelated departments
Add a warning sign without reviewing the incentive system
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Systems theory examines interactions and feedback among organizational components rather than isolating one person or department.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Focusing only on the individual misses the interacting conditions that may repeatedly produce the behavior.
The scenario demonstrates that production decisions affect safety outcomes.
A warning sign does not address the organizational feedback and incentive mechanisms described.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 21, systems management theory, pp. 510-513

questions.stem: After implementing a new permit process, the team compares field performance with objectives and identifies deviations. Which PDCA step is this?
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: The Check step measures and evaluates results against the planned objectives and criteria.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Planning establishes objectives and methods before implementation.
Doing is the implementation or pilot of the planned process.
Acting standardizes successful changes or corrects the system after evaluation.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)

questions.stem: A team has adequate pay and equipment but rarely reports improvement ideas. Which leadership action is most likely to strengthen intrinsic motivation?
options: Use public punishment for unsuccessful suggestions
Remove decision authority from the work group
Recognize useful contributions and give employees ownership of corrective-action projects
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Recognition, responsibility, achievement, and meaningful participation are stronger intrinsic motivators than additional control.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Surveillance may increase compliance but does not create ownership or recognition.
Punishing unsuccessful ideas discourages psychological safety and future participation.
Removing authority reduces responsibility and opportunities for achievement.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 21, motivation theories and management styles, pp. 505-514
